raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not want to spread myself too thin. My land is only 5 mu, and with just two people in the house, I will still do what feels steady and familiar. For me, the safest way is to keep most land in wheat-maize, because that gives grain and cash both, and I know this system well. But I will still keep some cotton, because if grain price is not good, cotton can still bring some money. People around me do the same kind of mix, and at my age I would rather follow what has worked than gamble on something new.

For wheat, I will keep the stronger land and give it a decent fertilizer base, not too little, because if wheat comes out weak in spring it is hard to fix. I usually put base fertilizer before sowing in October, then topdress once at jointing if the leaves look pale. Water from the well costs money, so I will not irrigate too many times, just at the key stages. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant maize right away on the same land. That turnaround is always tight, so I will do simple tillage or even just open rows quickly and sow. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area. Cotton needs more looking after and hand work, but on a small patch I can still manage it. I will not chase very high input, just enough fertilizer and a few irrigations if the summer turns dry. This year I want steady harvest, not big spending.
